I am a Ph.D. candidate in Economics at Yale University, working in industrial
organization and financial economics. My research studies competition in retail
banking: why depositors leave their money in low-yield accounts, and how much
market power that inertia gives banks. I combine dynamic structural models of
demand with large administrative datasets from the Banco Central do Brasil.

During my undergraduate studies, I spent a year as a macroeconomics research
intern at Bahia Asset Management, where I ran GDP and CPI nowcasting models and
maintained the cross-country database used by the research team and the trading
desk. I hold an M.A. in Economics from FGV EPGE and placed first nationally in
Brazil's 2019 ANPEC graduate entrance exam in economics.

You can reach me at [pedro.feijodemoraes@yale.edu](mailto:pedro.feijodemoraes@yale.edu).
